segments.text: in this video I want to answer the
question what is a business case think
of a set of scales like scales of
justice imagine on one side you've got
all the costs of your project all the
reasons one you might choose not to do
it the risks the things that could go
wrong the unexpected consequences the
disruptions that it will create and on
the other side are all the reasons to do
your projects the benefits the increased
revenue the reduction in costs the
improvement in service all the benefits
that you might achieve a business case
is a document that weighs the one
against the other and it's sometimes
called a cost-benefit analysis costs and
benefits are most easily calculated and
compared when you can express them in
financial terms and for some
organizations it's the financial costs
and benefits that set the standard for
evaluating a business case a business
case won't succeed unless the financial
benefits outweigh the financial costs
however it's not always possible to
express costs and benefits in financial
terms although it is still possible
sometimes to quantify them and of course
some costs and some benefits are hard to
quantify at all now a financial
assessment of the costs and benefits is
sometimes known as an investment
appraisal and each organization will
have its own standards and methodology
for conducting an investment appraisal
often these will involve sophisticated
mathematical and financial tools like
discounted cash flows looking at
measures like net present value and
internal rates of return
as indicators for how well the business
case is made if however you're not
skilled and experienced in financial
analysis if you don't have an accounting
or cost accounting background or you're
not skilled in manipulation of
sophisticated spreadsheets then my best
advice is to go to someone else who can
produce a discounted cash flow or follow
your organization's methodology the last
thing I want to say in defining what a
business case is is to suggest to you
that in common usage there are actually
two types of business case the first is
a piece of advocacy it makes the case
for your project it sets out the costs
and the benefits in order to demonstrate
that the project would be a good
investment for the organization that the
benefits outweigh the costs and
therefore the organization should sign
up to the business case and do the
project the second use of the term
business case is a more impartial use a
business case is a document that sets
out impartially the costs and the
benefits often of a number of options
for the project including the option to
do nothing or to do the minimum that is
required to meet regulation or
legislation or other internal
requirements this kind of business case
is a better decision-making tool because
it gives decision-makers a number of
options to select from and allows them
to feel confident that the evaluation of
each option is impartial and therefore
allows for a robust decision so in
answering the question what is a
business case the first thing you must
do is find out how the term business
case is being used within your
organization or within your client
sometimes it will be one sometimes it
will be the other but if you produce the
kind of business case you will not be
serving your organization or client well
and you will be setting yourself up for
problems
